questions.stem: A pricing JVM started with -Duser.timezone=Asia/Tokyo (UTC+09:00) puts java.sql.Date.valueOf(LocalDate.of(2026, 8, 14)) into a shared cache as its getTime() value. A reporting JVM started with -Duser.timezone=America/Chicago (UTC-05:00 in August) builds new java.sql.Date(millis) from that value and calls toLocalDate(). Which date does the reporting JVM get?

options.text: 2026-08-13, since the milliseconds hold the writer's midnight, which the reader's default zone puts on 13 August
options.says: midnight in Tokyo is 15:00Z on 13 August, which is 10:00 on 13 August in Chicago; toLocalDate reads in the default zone

options.text: 2026-08-13, since toLocalDate() reads a java.sql.Date in UTC, which puts the writer's midnight on 13 August
options.says: toLocalDate reads in the JVM's default zone, not in UTC; the date is right for the wrong reason

options.text: 2026-08-14, since toLocalDate() gives back the day that valueOf() was given, in whichever JVM it runs
options.says: valueOf stored midnight in Tokyo as milliseconds, and toLocalDate reads those milliseconds in the reading JVM's default zone

options.text: 2026-08-14, since the milliseconds of a java.sql.Date hold a day with no time of day attached
options.says: a java.sql.Date is midnight in the default zone of the JVM that made it, a moment like any other Date

origin.section: Timestamp and java.sql.Date Turn Local Values into Moments in the JVM's Default Zone

questions.stem: An idempotency filter remembers each processed event by storing Date.from(eventTime) in a legacy store. For a new delivery it checks stored.toInstant().equals(eventTime). An event with time 2026-11-02T16:40:05.250731Z is delivered twice. What does the filter do with the second delivery?

options.text: It drops the delivery as a duplicate, since Date.from() keeps the digits below the millisecond in a field of their own
options.says: that is Timestamp; a Date holds milliseconds only

options.text: It processes the event again, since the stored copy comes back with the digits below the millisecond cut off
options.says: Date.from truncates to .250, which does not equal .250731

options.text: It drops the delivery as a duplicate, since Instant.equals() ignores the digits below the millisecond
options.says: Instant.equals compares seconds and nanoseconds; the page's run printed equals: false

options.text: It processes the event again, since the stored copy comes back with the digits below the millisecond rounded up
options.says: Date.from truncates; it does not round

origin.section: Date and Instant Name the Same Moment, but a Date Keeps Only Milliseconds

questions.stem: A JVM started with -Duser.timezone=Europe/Berlin saves a slot at 2027-03-28T02:15 with Timestamp.valueOf(LocalDateTime) and later reads it back with toLocalDateTime() in the same JVM. That night Berlin's clocks go from 02:00 straight to 03:00. Which slot does it read?

options.text: 2027-03-28T02:15, since valueOf() and toLocalDateTime() are a matching pair and give back what they were given
options.says: the pair goes through the default zone, which has no 02:15 that night

options.text: 2027-03-28T03:15, since valueOf() moves a wall time that the default zone doesn't have an hour forward
options.says: the skipped wall time moves forward by the length of the gap

options.text: 2027-03-28T02:15, since a Timestamp keeps the date and time fields it was given rather than a moment
options.says: a Timestamp holds a moment; valueOf turns the local value into one in the default zone

options.text: 2027-03-28T03:15, since toLocalDateTime() reads the stored moment in UTC, which is an hour behind Berlin
options.says: toLocalDateTime reads in the JVM's default zone, not in UTC; the time is right for the wrong reason

origin.section: Timestamp and java.sql.Date Turn Local Values into Moments in the JVM's Default Zone

questions.stem: A scheduler builds its zone with TimeZone.getTimeZone(config.get("zone")), and the configuration says America/Sao_Paolo. What happens when the scheduler starts?

options.text: It fails at startup, since getTimeZone(String) throws for an ID it doesn't know
options.says: getTimeZone(String) answers an ID it cannot understand with GMT; only ZoneId.of throws

options.text: It fails at startup, since getTimeZone(String) checks every ID the way ZoneId.of() does
options.says: only ZoneId.of rejects an unknown ID; getTimeZone(String) falls back to GMT

options.text: It starts and runs in the JVM's zone, since getTimeZone(String) falls back to it for an ID it doesn't know
options.says: the fallback is GMT, not the JVM's default zone

options.text: It starts and runs in GMT, since getTimeZone(String) falls back to GMT for an ID it doesn't know
options.says: the page's run printed GMT for a misspelled ID

origin.section: Build a TimeZone from a ZoneId, So a Wrong ID Fails
